subject.title: [Bug]: Embedded runner "Network connection lost" when LLM generates a tool call with large parameters (param generation latency > underlying request timeout)

question: For OpenRouter-routed Anthropic models that stay silent while generating large tool-call arguments, should OpenClaw change default timeout behavior, add provider-specific argument streaming, or rely on explicit provider timeout configuration?
rationale: The durable fix trades off stall-detection latency, OpenRouter's OpenAI-compatible route, provider-specific streaming support, and existing timeout configuration semantics.

options.title: Live repro plus narrow provider fix
options.body: Require a live OpenRouter Anthropic repro and then implement the smallest runtime/provider change that avoids the silent-window failure for large tool arguments.

options.title: Document timeout configuration only
options.body: Keep current defaults and document `models.providers.openrouter.timeoutSeconds` as the supported mitigation for slow large-argument generations.

options.title: Relax cloud idle defaults
options.body: Raise or relax the default cloud idle watchdog and accept slower detection for genuinely stalled remote streams.

recommendation.title: Live repro plus narrow provider fix
recommendation.body: Require a live OpenRouter Anthropic repro and then implement the smallest runtime/provider change that avoids the silent-window failure for large tool arguments.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest recent history on embedded-runner timeout policy and provider-stream seams relevant to this decision.
